title: The quaker librarian came from the leavetakers. Blushing, his mask said
html_source:
Quaker librarian is mentioned twelve times in this episode. Lyster (his name) is only written twice. it is not surprising that he should have a mask, that is he is a nameless part of the chorus to the protaganists AE and Eglinton.

Joyce believed drama to be ‘literature in dialog form’ and ‘the interplay of passions to portray truth, drama is strife, evolution, movement in whatever way unfolded; it exists, before it takes form, independently; it is conditioned but not controlled by its scene’(Drama and Life. Occasional, Critical and Political Writings, Joyce).

This episode has many theatrical parallels and Joyce seems to paint Lyster as a minor character in the Irish literary pantomime.

The mention of “mask” is particularly telling: it probably alludes to Attic Tragedy where all members of the play wore masks that reflected the plays themes – sad and grand for tragedy, silly and buffoonish for comedy and satyr plays.

(Ancient Greek red figure painting of a tragic actor with a mask)

As the quaker librarian is a minor character, he would probably either be a messenger, slave, nurse or even chorus member. According to Aristotle (Poetics), Greek tragedy originally consisted solely of a chorus – a group of men who sung and danced religious themed songs – and a single actor who interacted with them. Supposedly, Aeschylus added a second actor, and Sophocles later added a third third (which Aeschylus used thereafter). Chorus literally means “dancing group”, signaling one of the original purposes of this theatrical branch.
